subsystem: Shared compressed state-channel and shard-checkpoint decoding
concrete_failure: An unauthenticated peer supplies a small Brotli payload that expands into a very large array before signature/authentication and before the existing decoded-size validation, exhausting native or JVM memory.
required_fix: Add a shared bounded streaming decompressor; reject compressed input before copying when it exceeds its lane cap; enforce decompressed byte and expansion-ratio limits before JSON/Scodec allocation; retain semantic size validators as a second bound.
red_tests: RED: maximum compressed and decompressed sizes succeed exactly at the boundary; boundary+1 is rejected before full allocation; a high-ratio Brotli bomb is rejected on HTTP, metagraph gossip, ChainSync-fed binary, and shard-checkpoint decode paths; invalid input never reaches signature or replay work.
dependencies: None; establish the shared byte-limit API used by TR-04, TR-05, and TR-06.

concrete_failure: A gossip flood is copied into an unbounded JVM queue and can cause unbounded callback backlog/fiber creation while expensive message handling falls behind, leading to heap exhaustion or validator liveness loss.
required_fix: Use bounded per-message-family queues, grpc-java manual inbound demand tied to available capacity, bounded parEvalMap concurrency, explicit overload drop/defer policy by family, and queue/drop/in-flight metrics.
red_tests: RED: flood every message family while handlers are blocked; queue depth and active handlers never exceed configured limits; manual demand stops; state-validity/checkpoint messages follow their ratified no-drop or pull-recovery policy; shutdown and reconnect leave no blocked producers or zombie streams.
dependencies: TR-01 for bounded decode at the consumer boundary; otherwise independently implementable.

subsystem: Shard checkpoint construction and GossipSub publication
concrete_failure: Count-bounded binary accumulation can construct a serialized checkpoint above GossipSub's 1 MiB frame limit; publication failure is swallowed while the exact oversized checkpoint remains held and republished forever, halting that shard.
required_fix: Select a deterministic per-metagraph-ordered prefix by exact encoded protobuf byte budget with fixed envelope/signature headroom; reject any individually unpublishable binary; return a typed publish result and release or deterministically rebuild a permanently unpublishable held checkpoint without skipping inputs.
red_tests: RED: adversarial binary sizes and map layouts produce the same maximal prefix on every node; encoded checkpoint stays within the 1 MiB GossipSub limit including all signatures; an individually oversized input is quarantined deterministically; permanent too-large publication does not retain/retry the same checkpoint forever; transient failures preserve byte identity.
dependencies: TR-01 for compressed/decompressed lane limits; freeze the actual GossipSub 1 MiB and gRPC 4 MiB framing constants in tests.

subsystem: Watchtower fraud-proof gossip and replay adjudication
concrete_failure: An unauthenticated sender can vary non-identity hint/witness bytes and repeatedly trigger full checkpoint replay for the same dispute, turning fraud adjudication into a remote CPU and data-fetch oracle.
required_fix: Require deterministic watchtower eligibility and bond/admission before replay; validate exact field lengths before crypto; single-flight and cache by (shardId, disputedCheckpointHash, metagraphAddress) excluding attacker-controlled hints; bound concurrent replay, work, fetches, and negative-cache lifetime.
red_tests: RED: many envelopes for one dispute with varied hints trigger at most one replay; ineligible/unbonded and wrong-length claims cause zero replay/fetch; distinct eligible disputes respect global and per-peer concurrency/work budgets; a failed or missing-data replay defers without slash and does not pin single-flight forever.
dependencies: TR-01 for bounded witness/envelope decoding; TR-02 for bounded gossip scheduling; protocol owner must ratify eligibility/bond and retry policy.

subsystem: Authenticated GlobalFollow HTTP server/client and changeset serialization
concrete_failure: An authenticated or compromised peer can request or return an unbounded accumulated changeset that is fully materialized and buffered on both server and client, exhausting heap/CPU before retention or response-size policy stops it.
required_fix: Define byte-based pagination with hash-bound continuation, cap requested ordinal span and output bytes before materialization, stream encoding/decoding, limit per-peer concurrent generation, authenticate before expensive work, and enforce symmetric server/client response caps before buffering.
red_tests: RED: a retained history larger than one page yields deterministic byte-bounded pages and verified continuation; oversized/malformed responses fail before full buffering; requested span and concurrent page generation are bounded; auth failure performs no changeset scan; client and server enforce the same maximum.
dependencies: TR-01 if compressed responses are retained; exact Phase-2 hash/reorg semantics and continuation preimage must already be frozen.

concrete_failure: A public client can stream an unbounded raw POST body that http4s materializes before the validator checks the decoded state-channel binary size, exhausting memory without possessing any metagraph key.
required_fix: Apply a streaming raw-entity byte cap at the route/server boundary before decoding; use TR-01 bounded decompression; separately cap decoded framework/custom content and reject trailing or multi-value bodies.
red_tests: RED: chunked and Content-Length bodies at limit succeed and limit+1 terminate early; missing or false Content-Length cannot bypass the cap; compressed bombs hit the decompressed cap; rejection occurs before Circe decode, hashing, signature checks, or queue insertion.
dependencies: TR-01 shared bounded decompression and lane limits; coordinate route-wide middleware placement with TR-05 without sharing mutable implementation ownership.

subsystem: Shard execution-certificate wire decoding and GL0 acceptance precheck
concrete_failure: A checkpoint can carry arbitrarily many duplicate or impossible committee signatures and oversized crypto fields; acceptance performs repeated expensive verification before the later distinct-signer quorum check rejects it.
required_fix: Before any signature/KES/VRF verification require signature count <= derived committee size, exact crypto field lengths, unique peer IDs, and membership; preserve canonical signer ordering and then run each expensive verification once.
red_tests: RED: duplicate peer IDs, count above committee size, nonmembers, and every wrong field length cause zero crypto-verifier calls; a canonical unique committee certificate verifies each signer exactly once; precheck result is permutation-independent or noncanonical ordering is rejected explicitly.
dependencies: TR-03 checkpoint wire-size budget and canonical signer envelope; replay-before-sign capability work must remain behaviorally unchanged.

concrete_failure: Although one ChainSync frame is capped at 16 MiB, inbound count/range policy is not enforced consistently and a peer can induce unbounded aggregate JVM work or stream many uncorrelated responses, exhausting CPU, disk, memory, or stream slots.
required_fix: Enforce per-peer rate/concurrency, request count/span, exact hash lengths, and overflow-safe range checks at the first sidecar boundary and again in the JVM; serve ranges in O(1) memory; cap aggregate response count/bytes/time and require exact request-to-response hash/range correlation.
red_tests: RED: >64 hashes, invalid hash lengths, reversed/overflowing/oversized ranges, excess request rate, excess response count/bytes, and unrequested hashes are rejected at the first boundary; maximum legal ranges stream in constant memory; slowloris reads/writes expire; cancellation releases every permit.
dependencies: Freeze the existing 16 MiB per-frame ceiling; reuse only immutable byte-limit primitives from TR-01, otherwise independently implementable.

concrete_failure: LATENT / NOT REMOTELY REACHABLE TODAY: a uint32 length above Int.MaxValue is narrowed with toInt and can become negative or otherwise enter invalid allocation/decoder behavior if a future transport permits such bytes.
required_fix: Replace unchecked uint32-to-Int mapping with an exmap that rejects values above the protocol maximum and Int.MaxValue before allocation; use lane-specific finite maxima rather than the representable uint32 maximum.
red_tests: RED: 0x7fffffff follows the configured protocol cap; 0x80000000 and 0xffffffff return typed decode failures without allocation or exception; current state-channel and currency record round trips remain canonical.
dependencies: Not remotely reachable under current GossipSub 1 MiB, gRPC 4 MiB, and ChainSync 16 MiB framing; schedule after TR-01 establishes lane maxima.

concrete_failure: LATENT / NOT REMOTELY REACHABLE TODAY: persisted Brotli bytes are fully decompressed into an unbounded array before Scodec decoding, so corrupted or adversarially replaced local storage could cause memory exhaustion during load.
required_fix: Use the shared bounded streaming decompressor with a persisted-value maximum and expansion-ratio limit; fail with a typed SerdeError before full allocation.
red_tests: RED: a local compressed bomb and boundary+1 persisted value return SerdeError without full allocation; boundary values and existing persisted fixtures round-trip byte-for-byte; no network test labels this path remotely reachable.
dependencies: TR-01 shared bounded decompression; current call sites are test/local persistence only and no remote reachability was found.
